author: GamingBolt
description:
It’s safe to say that the long absence of the Batman Arkham games has left a massive hole in the hearts of so many fans. Rocksteady didn’t just drop a great series; they delivered the definitive feeling of being Batman. It set the gold standard for any game that tried to replicate the same feeling, and honestly speaking, nothing has quite matched that lightning-in-a-bottle vibe since. 

However, the upcoming LEGO Batman: Legacy of the Dark Knight is stepping up to the mic, and it’s rather easy to dismiss this take on Batman as childish, but once you dig deep into the experience, it starts to feel like the same feeling, albeit from a different lens. 

Right from the fan service to the open-world of Gotham and the combat, there’s a lot of great stuff that has us stoked about LEGO Batman: Legacy of the Dark Knight.
title: LEGO Batman: Legacy of the Dark Knight Looks Like the Arkham Fix I Needed

author: GamingBolt
description:
We decided that Crimson Desert should get another pass after our initial review, courtesy of a bunch of changes that have seen the game evolve rapidly enough to justify the effort. 

And evolve it has. It's now an open-world that's far easier to navigate, and far more intuitive to engage with. Every issue that we had with it in our initial review is now resolved, and while a few of them continue to hold it back from a perfect score, there's now so much good about it that it comes pretty darn close to it. 

Crimson Desert more than earned its place among the finest open world titles out there. Join us to see why we think that's the case, and learn more about how its many patches have come together to make it a very attractive deal.

title: Crimson Desert Re-Review - The Comeback Is Real
